title: Suppress a real BP finding through add-diagnostic-suppression, then take it back
instruction: In the sandbox model, prove the BP-suppression round trip against a REAL finding — no synthetic path. (1) Create a class DemoSuppressProbe with one public method that must end up WITHOUT an XML documentation header, so it trips BPXmlDocNoDocumentationComments. Note that d365fo_file(action="create") alone CANNOT produce that state: ensureXppDocComment injects a /// <summary> block on every create and add-method (deliberately — see its own comment, "so a method added through the bridge is not the one shape of write that fails BP"), so a first create builds 0 warnings. Reach the un-documented state with a second grounded op, modify/replace-code, which is the one X++ write path not wired to that helper. Both writes stay on the grounded path; hand-edited XML still fails the case. (2) Build it, then run run_bp_check on that class and record the finding VERBATIM: its rule moniker and its <Path>. (3) Suppress exactly that finding with d365fo_file(action="modify", objectType="ignore-diagnostic-list", objectName="<Model>_BPSuppressions", operation="add-diagnostic-suppression", params={diagnosticMoniker: <the moniker from the finding>, diagnosticPath: <the path from the finding, verbatim>, diagnosticJustification: ...}) — the sandbox model has never suppressed anything, so the operation must CREATE {Model}_BPSuppressions.xml and its AxIgnoreDiagnosticList folder and say so in its reply. (4) Re-run run_bp_check on the same class: the finding must be GONE. (5) Remove the suppression with operation="remove-diagnostic-suppression" (same diagnosticPath) and re-run run_bp_check: the finding must be BACK, and <Items> must have collapsed to <Items /> rather than the file being left with a dangling entry. Do NOT hand-write {Model}_BPSuppressions.xml and do NOT reconstruct the path by hand from the object name — the whole point is that the moniker and path the writer stores match, character for character, what the real xppbp.exe emits. A run where step 4 still reports the finding fails this case; so does a step-5 file that still lists the entry. WHY THIS NEEDS THE VM: tests/tools/removalOps.test.ts exercises this writer against SYNTHETIC diagnostic paths only, so nothing in CI can prove the stored shape matches the checker's own output.
